svg.data-power-max-scope: 45 C, optics fully populated, 100% traffic load (HIG, both builds)
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO with optional holdover; ITU-T Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE); IEEE 1588v2 default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 (additional licence), T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC; Time Sensitive Networking (TSN); Class C timing accuracy. NOS integration is required to activate the specific feature, which the datasheet states with an asterisk against the whole block
svg.data-gnss: internal receiver for master clock implementations, supporting GPS/QZSS L1 C/A, GLONASS L10F, BeiDou B1, SBAS L1 C/A (WAAS, EGNOS, MSAS, GAGAN) and Galileo E1B/C at a minimum RF sensitivity of -166 dBm; passive and active antennas are auto-detected and an active antenna is fed up to 5 V DC / 150 mA
svg.data-breakout: the four SFP28 ports break out from 100G port 0; enabling them disables port 0
svg.data-compliance-programme: IEEE 802.1CM fronthaul; ITU-T G.8273.2 T-BC Class C
svg.data-optics-sfp28: 25G SFP28 SR/LR/ER and 10G SFP+ SR/LR/ER, up to 40 km
svg.data-timing-interfaces: GNSS in on SMA; 1PPS in/out on SMB; 10MHz in/out on SMB; ToD in/out on RJ45. Cable types the datasheet specifies: 50 ohm SMA coax with a 1/4-36UNS-2B connector for GNSS, 50 ohm SMB coax with a 10-32UNF-2A connector for 1PPS and 10MHz, shielded RJ45 for ToD
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232 at 115200 8N1 plus a micro-USB serial console (CP210x)
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A

The sixty-four lane lamps drawn here therefore keep ufispace/lane-led-quad@1's off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Nothing states whether the four lamps above a cage are four lanes, or a link/activity pair per breakout, or something else; the component's own provenance reaches the same conclusion from a different platform's guide.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["qsfp28","sfp28","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"The four SFP28 ports have no lamp of their own. Eight lamp groups are drawn in each band and there are eight QSFP columns, so none is spare, and the guide never mentions an SFP28 indicator. What the faceplate does say is that the first QSFP column's two lamp rows are painted yellow and orange, continuous with the SFP28 legend band, where every other column's are green - and the guide says those four ports are the breakout of port 0. The natural reading is that port 0's four lane lamps are the four SFP28 ports' lamps in breakout mode. It is a reading and not a statement, so the lamps here are attached to port-0 and port-1 and the SFP28 group carries no indicator.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["sfp28","port-leds"],"wanted":"a NOS LED table naming the breakout lamps, or a photograph of a unit with the breakout enabled and one SFP28 port linked","what":"sfp28-lamp-sharing"},{"note":"Three UfiSpace chassis guides dimension the same fan SKU three ways. This one's Component Physical Information table says 'Fan (W x D x H) 3.21 x 4.8 x 3.19 in (81.5 x 122 x 81 mm)'; the S9600-30DX guide says 81 x 113 x 81.5 and the S9600-28DX guide 80 x 113 x 81.5. The library part is 82.5 x 81.5, measured off a rear elevation, and my own elevation independently puts the repeating unit at 84.42 mm - face plus web - which supports it. The spread across the four numbers is 2.5 mm on width and 0.5 on height, under a pixel and a half at this figure's 2.96 px/mm, so no amount of re-measuring these figures resolves it. Reused rather than duplicated; the depth disagreement (122 against 113) is larger and is not measurable from any elevation at all.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ufispace/fan-803816@1","fans"],"wanted":"a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-803816-HI, or a caliper on the FRU","what":"fan-dimensions"},{"note":"ufispace/psu-162-dc@1 records that no held figure showed a DC unit seated in a chassis, and built its face from the AC unit's with a terminal block on the inlet's footprint - grille left, connector right. This device's intake HAS such a figure: the vendor rear product render (photos/s9600-32x-3-view) shows two DC supplies with two-hole lug pads behind a cover, and their whole face is MIRRORED relative to Figure 7's AC unit - connector on the left, grille and lamp and bail on the right. So the DC face is probably not the AC face with a substitution, and the existing component draws it the wrong way round. The component is not edited from here; the render is 520 px wide and is evidence of arrangement, not of geometry.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ufispace/psu-162-dc@1","psus"],"wanted":"an orthographic rear elevation or a close-up photograph of a DC-configured S9600-32X, good enough to dimension the terminal block","what":"dc-psu-face-mirrored"},{"note":"The panel numbers its ports inside the eight white lozenges in each lamp band, and at the best resolution the intake holds those numerals are two pixels tall and cannot be read. The numbers printed here are the column assignment the module-face numerals give, placed at the measured lozenge positions - the positions are measured and the digits are inferred. If the lozenges turn out to carry something else (a lane letter, a pair label), the positions stay right and the text is wrong.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["qsfp28","front"],"wanted":"a high-resolution front photograph, or a dimensioned faceplate drawing","what":"port-number-glyphs"},{"note":"No held document prints an orderable chassis part number. The datasheet names the product only as S9600-32X and its Available to Order block names only the two PSUs (PSU-162-DESR, PSU-162-AESR) and the one fan (FAN-803816-HI); the HIG prints no number anywhere. The S9510-28DC precedent applies - that model's SKUs came from the owner and from no held PDF - so the configurations here carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["base","ac","dc"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace ordering guide","what":"chassis-sku"},{"note":"At the junction between the yellow SFP28 legend band and the green QSFP28 band the faceplate prints a black up-triangle on the yellow and a white down-triangle on an orange strip, and the orange strip runs under the first column's lower lamp row. Both bands and both markers are drawn here because they are on the metal. Neither document explains the colour coding or the two triangles beyond the Port Overview sentence about the breakout, so what the orange specifically marks - the disabled port, the shared lanes, the lower row - is not stated.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"a legend or key for the faceplate colour coding","what":"orange-marker-meaning"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"3+1","redundancy-note":"3+1 - 3+1 hot-swappable (attrs fan-redundancy)"},"description":"the four rear fans, which the rear panel numbers 0 to 3","index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster along the bottom left - the out-of-band RJ45, the RS-232 console RJ45, the micro-USB serial console, the USB 3.0 maintenance port and the recessed reset button","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"every indicator that belongs to a particular port - one four-lamp cluster per QSFP28 port, in the band above or below its own cage","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 hot-swappable"},"description":"the two rear supplies, which the rear panel numbers PSU0 and PSU1","index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"description":"ports 0-31, the datasheet's '32 x 40/100G QSFP28 ports', in eight columns of two two-high stacked cages. They are the breakout of QSFP28 port 0 and enabling them disables it","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"status-leds":{"description":"the six chassis indicators the faceplate legends SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and ID, each with its own vocabulary from HIG section 10's Front Panel LED table","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"timing":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the timing block down the left edge - a GNSS antenna on SMA, 1PPS and 10MHz on SMB and ToD on RJ45. Three media, four jacks, one job: this is the block that makes an aggregation router a Class C grandmaster","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9600-32X","name":"s9600-32x","portfolio":{"family":"Open Aggregation Router","line":"Telecoms","series":"S9600 Series"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"attrs":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - Specifications, Performance, Environmental, Regulatory Compliance and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 2RU, 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm', weight 17.73 kg without FRU; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats both ('S9600-32X (W x D x H) 17.16 x 30 x 3.45 in (436 x 762 x 87.7mm)' and 'Chassis without FRU 39.09lb (17.73kg)'). 436 is the BODY and not a rack face: the HIG's Space Clearance section says 'The S9600-32X width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', so the ears are additional to 436 and are not drawn. 762 mm is the chassis without FRUs; the same section projects the fan handles 29 mm and the PSU handles 30 mm beyond it, which is why the clearance figure is larger than the depth."},"fan-part":{"note":"ufispace/fan-803816@1 is reused rather than a third near-duplicate built, and the reason is recorded because the tables disagree. THIS guide's Component Physical Information table gives the fan 81.5 x 122 x 81 mm (W x D x H); the S9600-30DX guide gives the same part number 81 x 113 x 81.5 and the S9600-28DX guide 80 x 113 x 81.5. Three chassis guides, one SKU, three tables. The library part is 82.5 x 81.5, measured off the S9600-30DX rear elevation, and my own elevation puts the repeating unit at 84.42 mm, which is that face plus a ~1.9 mm web - the same reading. The differences between the three tables are 1.5 mm and smaller, which is under a pixel and a half at this figure's 2.96 px/mm, so they cannot be resolved by measuring harder. See the fan-dimensions gap."},"grounding":{"note":"HIG section 8 - 'The location for securing the grounding lug is at the rear of the case and is covered with a protective label.' Figure 7 draws a silver plate with two round pads at x 348.0-358.5, y 6.0-38.6, an earth symbol beside it and a third round hole below, on the chassis strip between the fan bank and the PSU stack; HIG Figure 4's overview names it 'Ground Lug' with a leader to that strip. The plate is drawn as decor and the symbol as a placement: the lug itself ships loose in the accessory kit (5 lugs on the DC build, 1 on AC) and the pad is bare metal under a label until somebody bolts one on, so seating a lug component here would draw hardware the shipped chassis does not wear."},"lamp-band":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - the port lamps sit on a painted band above and below the cage block, py 71-88 and 262-280, i.e. 8.6-15.9 mm and 72.2-79.5 mm. Each band carries two rows of lamps, the upper row serving the upper port of every stacked pair and the lower row the lower: row centres measure 10.58 and 14.28 mm at the top and 73.80 and 77.11 at the bottom. Each row is four lamps on a 4.00 mm pitch, so ufispace/lane-led-quad@1 (14.4 x 2.6, four 2.4 mm lamps on 3.94) is placed unchanged - its pitch is within 1.5% of the measurement and its lamp diameter is a 3 px feature in this figure and is not independently resolvable."},"left-cluster":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - measured on Figure 8 at 2.9564 px/mm across and 2.976 down, and cross-read at 4x. Down the left edge, three gold jacks on one centreline (x 11.7-12.2): 1PPS SMB at y 6.4-13.4, 10MHZ SMB at 20.8-27.9 and the larger GNSS ANT SMA at 33.9-43.0, measuring 7.1, 7.1 and 9.5 mm across the nut - the datasheet's own split of '1 x GNSS input SMA, 1 x 1PPS input/output SMB, 1 x 10MHz input/output SMB', not a family assumption. To their right the ToD RJ45 (x 22.2-38.5, y 26.7-41.7) and a PORTRAIT USB 3.0 A receptacle (x 42.3-49.5, y 27.7-41.3), with the reset pinhole at (30.4, 46.6) below them. Along the bottom: the six-lamp status block at x 11.16-13.87 on a 2.45 mm pitch inside a white legend panel at x 6.4-10.2, then the micro-USB console slot at x 18.2-26.2, the RJ45 console at 29.4-44.7 and the RJ45 management jack at 49.4-65.3, the last identified by the two green lamps colour detection finds in its lower corners."},"lifecycle":{"note":"searched 28 August 2026 - 'UfiSpace S9600-32X end of life end of sale announcement'. No notice from UfiSpace or any reseller appears; the vendor's product page, the FAQ page and the S9600 brochure are all live. NDX advertises lifecycle dates behind its commercial tiers and publishes none. none-announced is a real finding rather than an absence of looking."},"panel-metal":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - THE BRIGHT SHELLS ARE PANEL, NOT PART. std/qsfp-ganged and std/sfp-ganged draw the aperture and what is behind it and stop at the metal, so the light shell each ganged block sits in is drawn here as panel.decor: one 39.0 x 56.3 mm plate per two-column QSFP block at x 93.25, 135.70, 178.15 and 220.60, and one 30.8 x 26.6 plate under the SFP28 quad at 53.1. Without them thirty-six dark apertures sit on a dark faceplate and vanish. The thin dark seam at y 43.9 is the join between each block's upper and lower two-high cage, which the figure draws as a 1-2 px line. The same rule puts a silver pill behind the portrait USB-A and the micro-USB, whose std/ parts draw only the opening."},"port-numbering":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - NUMBERING RUNS DOWN EACH COLUMN and the numbers are printed on the LAMP BAND, not on the cages. Figure 8 prints '0 2 / 1 3', '4 6 / 5 7' and so on across the upper half and '16 18 / 17 19' across the lower, so column c carries port 2c over 2c+1 in the upper pair and 16+2c over 17+2c in the lower - eight columns, thirty-two ports, matching the guide's Port Overview table ('0 ~ 31, QSFP28, 40/100G'). But those numerals are drawn on the schematic module faces, where a seated transceiver would cover them. The panel's own numbering is on the eight white lozenges in the lamp band, one per column, each split into an upper and a lower half: colour detection puts them at 94.0, 132.2, 136.3, 174.9, 178.9, 217.3, 221.6 and 260.3 mm - a single lozenge at each end of the port block and a pair at each of the three inter-block webs, which is exactly eight for eight columns, and each sits on the OUTER edge of its own column. The numerals inside them are 2 px tall in the best figure held and cannot be read; they are drawn here from the column assignment above, which the module-face numerals and the NDX interface list (ce0-ce31, xe0-xe3) both give independently."},"port-pitch":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - AND TAKEN FROM THE LAMPS, NOT THE CAGE FILLS. Figure 8 draws a transceiver face inside every aperture, and those fills are wider than the port pitch; measuring between them puts a gutter down each block. The ruler used here is the lane-lamp cluster, which repeats once per PORT COLUMN: colour detection finds 32 lamps per row in the upper band at centres 294.5 to 763.0 px, in eight groups of four on a 11.83 px (4.00 mm) lamp pitch. The eight group centres give a within-block column pitch of 19.11, 19.11, 18.95 and 19.11 mm and a block-to-block pitch of 42.45, 42.53 and 42.37 mm. 19.0 mm is the ganged QSFP pitch std/qsfp-ganged records from a TE 2322551-4 cage, so the measurement corroborates the standard rather than the other way round, and the manifest carries 19.00 within a block and 42.45 between blocks. Column 0's left edge lands at 94.00 mm."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet 'Typical power: 335 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. The HIG states the maximum twice, once per build: 'The maximum system power consumption is 609 watts' in the DC section and '621.3 watts' in the AC section, and unusually BOTH are qualified - 'Testing criteria for maximum power are as follows: Temperature 45C, Optics: full populated, Traffic: 100% load' appears under each. 621.3 is carried as power-max-w because max means the highest, and the 12.3 W difference is recorded here rather than as a conflict: they are two builds, not two readings. The 1600 W that appears beside them is a provisioning instruction ('a reserve of at least 1600 watts on each power circuit') and is the supply's rating, not a draw. These are the vendor's figures as the vendor states them and are NOT reconciled against the module set; the fans publish no draw, so any total built from the modelled modules is a floor."},"psu-build":{"note":"THE GUIDE DRAWS AC AND THE PRODUCT RENDER SHOWS DC, and the two are not blended. HIG Figure 7's rear elevation - the only orthographic rear the intake holds - draws both bays with an appliance inlet, a mesh grille to its left, a green lamp and a red bail, which is ufispace/psu-162-ac@1 exactly. The vendor's rear product render (photos/s9600-32x-3-view) shows a DC build instead: two two-hole lug pads behind a cover where the inlet is, and the whole face MIRRORED, grille on the right. The manifest models the documented build - AC, from the figure that passes the gate - and the dc configuration swaps in ufispace/psu-162-dc@1, whose own contract records that no figure of a seated DC unit was available to it. That render is such a figure and it disagrees with that part's layout; the part is not edited from here. See the dc-psu-face-mirrored gap."},"rear-layout":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing, and it passes the same gate the front does. Figure 7's rear elevation measures 1292 x 261 px, 0.44% from the stated aspect. The four fan modules repeat on a measured 84.42 mm pitch, taken from the status lamp, which is a feature that repeats once per module: lamp centres at 18.39, 102.76, 187.29 and 271.65 mm, y 23.5. ufispace/fan-803816@1 carries its lamp at (16.2, 18.5) in a 82.5 x 81.5 face, which puts the bay origins at x 0.90 + 84.42k and y 3.70. The PSU stack is anchored the same way: its two lamps sit at x 384.0 and y 7.9 and 50.4, and ufispace/psu-162-ac@1 carries its lamp at (7.0, 3.4) in a 50.5 x 40.0 face, giving bay origins (375.5, 3.0) and (375.5, 45.5) and a 42.5 mm stack pitch. NOTE this is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT reading of the same chassis: the S9600-30DX model measured its own guide's Figure 7 and got an 84.4 mm fan pitch and a 43 mm PSU pitch. The agreement is corroboration because the two measurements were taken from two different documents, not copied."},"row-grid":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - four aperture rows on ONE 15.00 mm grid, and the SFP28 quad sits on rows 1 and 2 of it. Profiling a column strictly inside a cage gives bezel separators at py 131.5, 177 and 221.5 with the block running 89 to 265, i.e. row centres 44.67 px (15.01 mm) apart - 15.0 to a hundredth, which is also the belly-to-belly pitch std/sfp-ganged records from a TE 2007562-6. Aperture tops are therefore 17.05, 32.05, 47.05 and 62.05 mm. The SFP28 shell measures 16.13 to 42.34 mm vertically; putting its two 10.4 mm apertures on grid rows 1 and 2 predicts a shell bottom of 42.45, which is 0.11 mm from the measurement, so the quad is placed on the same grid rather than on a second one of its own."},"scale-gate":{"note":"BOTH GUIDE ELEVATIONS PASS GATE 1, which is why this model takes absolute geometry off them rather than only fractions. HIG Figure 8's port overview (extracted as fig-0014) has a front face of 1289 x 261 px against the stated 436 x 87.7 mm chassis - aspect 4.939 against a true 4.9715, 0.65% out - giving 2.9564 px/mm across and 2.976 px/mm down. HIG Figure 7's rear elevation (fig-0013) measures 1292 x 261 px, aspect 4.950, 0.44% out, at 2.9633 and 2.976 px/mm. The two scales are derived independently from two figures and agree to 0.2%. The three product renders do NOT pass: the front render is 520 px wide, a sixth of the guide figure's resolution, and is used for colour and for the DC build only."},"second-party":{"note":"NetBox Labs NDX carries this device type (netboxlabs.com/ndx/ufispace/ ufispace-s9600-32x, last verified 4 April 2026) and was read for COMPLETENESS only. The guide's Port Overview says so in words: ports 0 to 3 (yellow labels) are a breakout of 100G port 0 (green label), and enabling ports 0 to 3 disables that 100G port 0. The faceplate says it in paint: the quad's legend band is yellow, and the yellow continues right past the quad to cover the lamp rows of the FIRST QSFP column and only that column, with an orange strip under its lower row. Every other column's lamps sit on green. Counting settles that the yellow-and-orange lamps belong to the QSFP column and not to the quad: eight lamp groups are drawn and there are eight QSFP columns, so none is spare for the SFP28 ports, which carry no lamp of their own. The patch is the printing's own footprint plus 0.4 mm, which is what the S9610-36D's front render measures: its slots stop 0.4 mm outside each lamp cluster and resume 0.4 mm past it.
